nodes.label: README
nodes.description: Project entry point: Scrapy is a cross-platform web scraping framework for Python 3.10+, maintained by Zyte; shows `pip install scrapy` and links to the docs and contributing guide.

nodes.label: Install pointer
nodes.description: Stub that points to the local and online installation guide.

nodes.label: Contributing pointer
nodes.description: Stub that links to the online contributing guidelines and asks not to use the issue tracker for support questions.

nodes.label: Security policy
nodes.description: Only the 2.19.x series receives security fixes; vulnerabilities are reported through GitHub security advisories.

nodes.label: Contributing to Scrapy
nodes.description: How to report bugs, find work, write and submit patches; coding style (Ruff via pre-commit), documentation policies (autodoc, versionadded) and running tests with tox and pytest.

nodes.label: Scrapy at a glance
nodes.description: Short walk-through of a quotes spider run with `scrapy runspider`, explaining the asynchronous request scheduling and the features Scrapy offers.

nodes.label: Installation guide
nodes.description: Supported Python versions (3.10+, CPython or PyPy), installation with pip or conda, key dependencies (lxml, parsel, w3lib, Twisted, cryptography), optional extras and platform notes.

nodes.label: Scrapy tutorial
nodes.description: Step-by-step guide: create a project, write a spider, extract data with CSS/XPath selectors, store it with feed exports and follow links.

nodes.label: Architecture overview
nodes.description: The data flow controlled by the engine (spider, scheduler, downloader, middlewares, item pipelines), one paragraph per component, and the use of Twisted for event-driven networking.

nodes.label: Scrapy's building blocks
nodes.description: Quick map of spiders, items, settings, middlewares, pipelines and extensions: which problem each solves and when to use it.

nodes.label: Components
nodes.description: Defines a Scrapy component as any class built with build_from_crawler, lists the settings that take components, and explains from_crawler, component settings and enforcing requirements.

nodes.label: Settings
nodes.description: How settings are designated and populated with six precedence levels, component priority dictionaries, pre-crawler/reactor/logging special settings, and the reference of built-in settings.

nodes.label: Spiders
nodes.description: The crawl cycle (start, callbacks, items, pipelines), the scrapy.Spider base class, spider arguments, start requests and the generic spiders CrawlSpider, XMLFeedSpider, CSVFeedSpider and SitemapSpider.

nodes.label: Items
nodes.description: The item types supported through itemadapter (dicts, Item, dataclasses, attrs, Pydantic), declaring Item subclasses and Fields, and writing code that supports any item type.

nodes.label: Item Pipeline
nodes.description: Writing pipeline components (process_item, open_spider, close_spider), examples (validation, JSON lines, MongoDB, duplicates), activation through ITEM_PIPELINES and common pitfalls.

nodes.label: Downloader Middleware
nodes.description: Activating and ordering downloader middlewares, the process_request/process_response/process_exception hooks, and the reference of every built-in downloader middleware.

nodes.label: Spider Middleware
nodes.description: Activating and ordering spider middlewares, the process_spider_input/output/exception and process_start hooks, BaseSpiderMiddleware and the built-in spider middlewares.

nodes.label: Extensions
nodes.description: Extensions as wildcard components loaded once per crawler from EXTENSIONS, a sample extension, and the built-in general-purpose and debugging extensions.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.description: How to connect to Scrapy signals, handler order, asynchronous handlers, and the reference of engine, item, spider, request and response signals.

nodes.label: Requests and Responses
nodes.description: The Request and Response classes and subclasses, request fingerprints, callbacks and errbacks, Request.meta special keys and stopping a download.

nodes.label: Selectors
nodes.description: Extracting data with XPath and CSS selectors, a thin wrapper over parsel; nesting, regular expressions, XPath tips, and the Selector/SelectorList reference.

nodes.label: Feed exports
nodes.description: Exporting scraped items to files: serialization formats, storage backends (local, FTP, S3, GCS, stdout), item filtering, post-processing and the FEEDS family of settings.

nodes.label: Item Exporters
nodes.description: Using and customizing item exporters (start_exporting, export_item, finish_exporting), field serialization and the built-in exporters for JSON, CSV, XML, pickle and more.

nodes.label: Item Loaders
nodes.description: Populating items with Item Loaders, input and output processors, nested loaders and reuse; Scrapy's ItemLoader extends the itemloaders library with response support.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.description: The scheduler component that stores requests from the engine and feeds them back; overriding it with SCHEDULER, BaseScheduler, the default Scheduler and the priority queues.

nodes.label: asyncio
nodes.description: Native asyncio support: the asyncio reactor (default), pre-installed reactor problems, mixing Deferreds and asyncio, and the experimental mode without a Twisted reactor with its limitations.

nodes.label: Coroutines
nodes.description: Which callables may be `async def` (start, callbacks, pipeline and middleware methods, signal handlers) and how to use Deferred-based APIs from coroutines.

nodes.label: Add-ons
nodes.description: The add-on system that bundles and configures components through the ADDONS setting, writing add-ons with update_settings, fallbacks and examples.

nodes.label: Download handlers
nodes.description: Components that download requests per URL scheme (DOWNLOAD_HANDLERS), lazy handlers, writing your own, and the built-in HTTP (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, aiohttp, httpx) and non-HTTP handlers.

nodes.label: Core API
nodes.description: API for extension and middleware developers: Crawler, Settings, SpiderLoader, Signals, Stats Collector and Engine APIs.

nodes.label: Jobs: pausing and resuming crawls
nodes.description: Persisting a crawl in a JOBDIR (scheduler queues, dupefilter, spider state) so it can be paused and resumed, and the persistence gotchas.

nodes.label: Security
nodes.description: Scrapy defaults with security implications (untrusted responses, memory limits, TLS verification, unencrypted and local protocols, telnet and remote control, credential leakage, job state) and how to harden them.

nodes.label: Spiders Contracts
nodes.description: Testing spider callbacks with @-contracts in their docstrings (@url, @returns, @scrapes...), run by `scrapy check`, and writing custom contracts.

nodes.label: Stats Collection
nodes.description: The Stats Collector key/value facility available through Crawler.stats, common uses, the available collectors and the reference of stats Scrapy sets.

nodes.label: AutoThrottle extension
nodes.description: Design goals and algorithm of the extension that adjusts download delays from server latency, and its settings.

nodes.label: SEP index
nodes.description: Explains that the sep/ folder holds Scrapy Enhancement Proposals, mostly migrated from the old Trac wiki.

nodes.label: SEP-002: List fields API
nodes.description: Obsolete proposal (by SEP-008) for an API to handle list-valued item fields.

nodes.label: SEP-008: Item Loaders
nodes.description: Final proposal for the Item Parser API, implemented with variations as Item Loaders: input/output processors and add_value/add_xpath/populate_item.

nodes.label: SEP-009: Singleton removal
nodes.description: Proposal to replace the Scrapy 0.7 singletons (engine, manager, extensions, stats, signals) with members of a single root Crawler object.

nodes.label: SEP-012: Spider name
nodes.description: Final proposal to identify spiders by a `name` attribute and merge domain_name/extra_domain_names into allowed_domains.

nodes.label: SEP-013: Middlewares refactoring
nodes.description: Unfinished proposal to fix inconsistencies in spider, downloader and scheduler middleware hooks, such as missing exception hooks on the way in.

nodes.label: SEP-014: CrawlSpider v2
nodes.description: Proposal to rewrite CrawlSpider with matcher objects and separate request extractors/processors; partially implemented and then discarded for lack of use.

nodes.label: SEP-017: Spider Contracts
nodes.description: Proposal for a lightweight design-by-contract mechanism to test spider callbacks from tags in their docstrings.

nodes.label: SEP-018: Spider Middleware v2
nodes.description: Draft of a new spider middleware architecture with reusable, possibly per-spider components (process_response, process_error, process_request).

nodes.label: SEP-019: Per-spider settings
nodes.description: Final proposal, implemented with variations, for per-spider settings, setting priorities and the crawl process cleanup (from_crawler, spider loader).

nodes.label: Twisted as the networking engine
nodes.description: Scrapy is written on Twisted, an event-driven networking framework, so it downloads with non-blocking asynchronous code for concurrency instead of threads.

nodes.label: asyncio reactor by default
nodes.description: TWISTED_REACTOR defaults to AsyncioSelectorReactor so that asyncio and asyncio-based libraries can be used in any coroutine; new projects need no setup.

nodes.label: Running without a Twisted reactor
nodes.description: TWISTED_REACTOR_ENABLED=False runs Scrapy directly on the asyncio loop (allowing several AsyncCrawlerProcess runs, avoiding SelectorEventLoop limits), switching HTTP(S) to the aiohttp handler and disabling reactor-only features.

nodes.label: Settings precedence levels
nodes.description: Settings are populated from six sources with numeric priorities (default 0, command 10, addon 15, project 20, spider 30, cmdline 40), so overriding does not depend on load order.

nodes.label: Component priority dictionaries
nodes.description: Middlewares, pipelines, extensions and add-ons are enabled with dicts of component to integer order, merged with a *_BASE setting; None disables a built-in component.

nodes.label: Middleware hook architecture
nodes.description: HTTP-level and spider-level customization goes through ordered chains of hooks between the engine and the downloader or the spiders; requests traverse them in increasing order and responses or output in decreasing order.

nodes.label: Crawler as the single root object
nodes.description: Instead of global singletons, every core component hangs off a Crawler that components receive through from_crawler; it is the only way for them to reach settings, signals and stats.

nodes.label: Any item type through itemadapter
nodes.description: Scrapy accepts dicts, Item objects, dataclasses, attrs and Pydantic models via itemadapter, and code that receives items should work with all of them.

nodes.label: Selectors as a thin wrapper over parsel
nodes.description: Selectors delegate to the stand-alone parsel library (built on lxml) and only add integration with Response objects, giving lxml speed and accuracy.

nodes.label: Item Loaders with input/output processors
nodes.description: Populating items is separated from the item container: loaders run input processors on added values and output processors when building the item; the Item Parser API of SEP-008 was implemented as Item Loaders, now based on the itemloaders library.

nodes.label: Spiders identified by name
nodes.description: Spiders get a unique `name` attribute as identifier and a single allowed_domains list, so several spiders can scrape the same domain.

nodes.label: Per-spider settings
nodes.description: Spiders may override settings before the crawler uses them (custom_settings, update_settings) and are built by the crawler via from_crawler; implemented with variations, custom_settings ended up a class attribute.

nodes.label: Extensions as wildcard components
nodes.description: Logic that fits no specific role (stats, memory limits, telnet) goes into extensions, loaded once per crawler from EXTENSIONS and hooked in through signals.

nodes.label: Add-ons bundle component configuration
nodes.description: An add-on enables and configures related middlewares, extensions or pipelines in one place through the ADDONS setting, for a plug-and-play experience.

nodes.label: Download handlers chosen per URL scheme
nodes.description: The downloader picks a handler by the request URL scheme from DOWNLOAD_HANDLERS merged with DOWNLOAD_HANDLERS_BASE; unknown schemes raise NotSupported.

nodes.label: Downloader-aware priority queue by default
nodes.description: The scheduler defaults to DownloaderAwarePriorityQueue because it works better than ScrapyPriorityQueue when crawling many domains in parallel.

nodes.label: Spider contracts in docstrings
nodes.description: Spider callbacks are tested with design-by-contract tags in their docstrings (sample URL, expected items/requests), run quickly without a full crawl.

nodes.label: CrawlSpider v2 discarded
nodes.description: A rewrite of CrawlSpider with matcher objects and separate request extractors/processors was partially implemented and then discarded for lack of use; the Rule/LinkExtractor design stayed.

nodes.label: Spider Middleware v2
nodes.description: Proposed spider middleware API with reusable global or per-spider components; never completed, the current API keeps process_spider_input/output/exception.

nodes.label: Stats API always available
nodes.description: The Stats Collector API works even when stats collection is disabled (it just collects nothing), so collecting a stat takes one line and costs almost nothing when off.

nodes.label: API reference from docstrings
nodes.description: API reference lives in docstrings pulled with Sphinx autodoc, topics go in docs/, and docs of deprecated features are removed when they are deprecated.

nodes.label: Defaults optimized for scraping, not hardening
nodes.description: Scrapy keeps permissive defaults (e.g. no TLS certificate verification, unencrypted protocols allowed) because stricter ones break valid scraping cases; the security page explains how to harden them.

nodes.label: Scrapy data flow
nodes.description: The nine-step loop run by the engine: requests from the spider go through the scheduler and downloader middlewares to the downloader, responses back through spider middlewares to callbacks, items to pipelines, until the scheduler is empty.

nodes.label: Execution engine
nodes.description: Core component that controls the data flow between all other components and fires events when actions occur.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.description: Component that receives requests from the engine, stores them in memory or disk queues and returns the next request when the engine asks.

nodes.label: Downloader
nodes.description: Component that fetches web pages through download handlers and feeds the responses to the engine.

nodes.label: Spider
nodes.description: User class that defines which requests to send and how to parse their responses into items and further requests; one per site or group of sites.

nodes.label: Request
nodes.description: An HTTP request generated in spiders that travels through the system to the downloader; carries callback, errback, meta and priority.

nodes.label: Response
nodes.description: The downloaded result of a request, returned to the spider that issued it; text subclasses add selectors and encoding handling.

nodes.label: Callback and errback
nodes.description: Spider functions called with the response of a request (or with the failure), which return or yield items and new requests.

nodes.label: Item
nodes.description: A key-value object holding scraped data; any type supported by itemadapter can be used.

nodes.label: Item pipeline
nodes.description: Ordered chain of components that receive every scraped item to clean, validate, deduplicate or store it, or drop it with DropItem.

nodes.label: Downloader middleware chain
nodes.description: Ordered hooks between the engine and the downloader that process every request and response at the HTTP level (proxies, retries, redirects, caching).

nodes.label: Spider middleware chain
nodes.description: Ordered hooks between the engine and spider callbacks that process responses going in and items/requests coming out.

nodes.label: Extension
nodes.description: A component with no specific role in the data flow, used for anything else (stats, memory limits, telnet), usually driven by signals.

nodes.label: Signal
nodes.description: Events Scrapy sends (engine_started, item_scraped, spider_idle...) that handlers connect to, delivering only the arguments the handler accepts.

nodes.label: Component
nodes.description: Any class Scrapy builds with build_from_crawler, optionally through a from_crawler class method that gives it the crawler.

nodes.label: Crawler
nodes.description: The object that wires settings, signals, stats, extensions and the engine for one spider run, and the entry point of the core API.

nodes.label: Setting priority
nodes.description: Each setting value carries a priority (default, command, addon, project, spider, cmdline) and only a value of equal or higher priority overrides it.

nodes.label: Add-on
nodes.description: A class enabled in ADDONS that adjusts settings to enable and configure a set of components.

nodes.label: Download handler
nodes.description: Component that downloads requests for one URL scheme (http, https, ftp, s3, file, data) and produces responses.

nodes.label: Request fingerprint
nodes.description: A hash that identifies a request, used by the duplicate filter, the HTTP cache and other components to tell requests apart.

nodes.label: Duplicate request filter
nodes.description: Filter that drops requests whose fingerprint was already seen, configured by DUPEFILTER_CLASS and persisted in JOBDIR.

nodes.label: Selector
nodes.description: Object that selects parts of an HTML/XML document with XPath or CSS expressions and extracts data from them.

nodes.label: Item loader
nodes.description: Helper that populates items by passing extracted values through input and output processors.

nodes.label: Feed export
nodes.description: Built-in export of scraped items to feeds in several formats and storage backends, configured with FEEDS.

nodes.label: Item exporter
nodes.description: Serializer that writes items to a file in a format (JSON, JSON lines, CSV, XML, pickle, marshal); used by feed exports.

nodes.label: Stats collection
nodes.description: Key/value counters collected during a crawl and accessible through Crawler.stats.

nodes.label: Spider contract
nodes.description: A docstring tag (@url, @returns, @scrapes...) that states what a callback must produce for a sample page, checked by `scrapy check`.

nodes.label: Job persistence (JOBDIR)
nodes.description: Storing scheduler queues, seen requests and spider state on disk so a crawl can be paused and resumed.

nodes.label: Crawling rule
nodes.description: In CrawlSpider, a Rule pairs a link extractor with a callback and follow behaviour to crawl links automatically.

nodes.label: AutoThrottle
nodes.description: Automatic adjustment of download delay and concurrency from the observed server latency.

nodes.label: Twisted reactor
nodes.description: The single per-process Twisted event loop Scrapy runs on; reactor settings are fixed once it is installed.

nodes.label: SEP-002 header says SEP 3
nodes.description: The metadata table of sep/sep-002.rst gives the number 3 while its title says SEP-002; sep-003.rst also declares SEP 3, so two proposals share a number.

nodes.description: SEP-009 is marked as a document being written, yet its proposal is in place: Crawler is the root object holding settings, signals, stats, extensions and engine.

nodes.label: Components page omits some component settings
nodes.description: components.rst defines a component as any class built with build_from_crawler and lists the settings that take one, but omits ITEM_PROCESSOR (which settings.rst calls a component), LOG_FORMATTER and REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS, all built with build_from_crawler.
